newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse announces plan to split in two.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse announces plan to split in two.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp., as widely expected, said Wednesday it will split into two companies by spinning off its industrial business in a tax-free distribution to shareholders.

The company, which plans to concentrate on its rapidly growing television and radio businesses, said the $4.6 billion spinoff will create a new Pittsburgh-based company that will be called Westinghouse Electric Co., or WELCO.
Westinghouse, which plans to eliminate 1,100 jobs as part of the restructuring, said it was taking a one-time charge of $125 million to cover severance and related costs.
Westinghouse's separate broadcast company, to be headquartered in New York, will have its own board of directors and be headed by current Westinghouse Chairman Michael Jordan.
A new chief executive will be named for WELCO.

After the spinoff, Westinghouse Electric Corp., the current parent company, will consist of the CBS Inc. television network, Group W Satellite Communications Co., a cable television marketing and distribution company, and Infinity Broadcasting, which Westinghouse is acquiring.
Westinghouse also plans to offer up to 20 percent of its Thermo King refrigeration unit in a public stock offering.

The company also said it was divesting its Security Systems businesses and restructuring its Pittsburgh corporate headquarters and other industrial businesses to cut WELCO's overhead and operating costs significantly.

Westinghouse said its breakup, which is expected to take nine months, is subject to a ruling from the Internal Revenue Service that the transaction will not be taxable to Westinghouse's shareholders or to Westinghouse.
The company said it opted for the plan because its board expects the approach will maximize the long-term after-tax value for Westinghouse shareholders.
The broadcast company will retain all debt obligations of the current Westinghouse Electric Corp., as well as the company's $1.8 billion tax-beneficial net operating loss.
Westinghouse stock closed Tuesday at $20.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
